blocks.orig: The population of Tanzania is almost 60 million. One of Africa’s most ethnically diverse countries, around 125 different ethnic groups live in Tanzania, with more than 100 different languages spoken nationwide.
blocks.html: Tanzania has a population of close to 60 million and is among the most ethnically varied nations on the African continent: some 125 distinct ethnic groups call it home, and over 100 languages are in use across the country.

blocks.orig: The Tanzanian people are well-known for their hospitality, often warmly welcoming tourists to experience their beautiful nature, wildlife and culture. Meeting the locals is one of the best ways to really learn more about a country and its culture and is well recommended on your Tanzania discovery!
blocks.html: Tanzanians are famous for their hospitality and are generally quick to welcome visitors who come to enjoy their beautiful nature, wildlife and culture. Spending time with local people is one of the finest ways to get to know a country and its culture properly, and we warmly recommend it as part of your Tanzania adventure.

blocks.orig: Most international travellers will need a visa to travel to Tanzania. Your visa can be requested online through the official visa website from the Tanzanian government. Please note that this is the only official link for Tanzania visa applications.
blocks.html: The majority of international visitors need a visa for Tanzania. You can apply for it online via the Tanzanian government's official visa website. Bear in mind that this is the only official channel for Tanzania visa applications.

blocks.orig: It is also possible to get a tourist or business visa for a single entry on arrival at the main ports of entry to Tanzania. This visa for Tanzania is valid for three months. You may be asked to provide proof of your return journey, and costs are $50 per person, US Citizens $100 per person.
blocks.html: Alternatively, you can pick up a single-entry tourist or business visa when you arrive at one of Tanzania's main ports of entry. Such a visa stays valid for three months. Be prepared to show evidence of your return trip; the fee is $50 per person, or $100 per person if you hold US citizenship.

blocks.html: If you arrange your Tanzania trip with us as Tanzania experts, we walk you through every stage of the visa and paperwork process.

blocks.orig: Passports should have at least six months of validity after the final day of travel.
blocks.html: Your passport must remain valid for at least six months beyond the last day of your trip.

blocks.orig: What vaccinations are needed for Tanzania?
blocks.html: Which vaccinations do you need for Tanzania?

blocks.orig: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is only required for travellers one year of age and older coming from – or who are in airport transit for more than 12 hours within – a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.
blocks.html: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is only compulsory for travellers aged one year and above who arrive from – or spend more than 12 hours in airport transit in – a country where there is a risk of yellow fever transmission.

blocks.orig: In addition to standard vaccinations such as MMR and TDP, the CDC and WHO recommend vaccinations for Tanzania, such as Hepatitis A, hepatitis B, and typhoid. Yellow fever and rabies vaccinations are also recommended depending on the traveller’s activities.
blocks.html: Beyond routine vaccinations such as MMR and TDP, the CDC and WHO advise vaccinations for Tanzania including Hepatitis A, hepatitis B and typhoid. Depending on what you plan to do, yellow fever and rabies vaccinations may also be recommended.

blocks.orig: As with all international travel, we always advise you to consult your physician for professional health advice before travelling to Tanzania.
blocks.html: As for any international trip, our standing advice is to see your doctor for professional health guidance before you travel to Tanzania.

blocks.orig: The local currency is the Tanzanian shilling, although dollars and euros are also accepted in most touristic places in Tanzania.
blocks.html: The Tanzanian shilling is the local currency, but in most tourist spots around Tanzania dollars and euros are accepted as well.

blocks.orig: There are over 100 different languages spoken in Tanzania. The official languages, however, are Swahili and English. You can expect all your Your Tanzania Trip guides and hosts to speak English, but if you’re looking to learn a few words of Swahili before your trip, check out our list of top 25 useful words in Swahili!

blocks.orig: Swahili and English are the official languages in Tanzania, but Swahili is spoken by almost everyone. In the tourism sector, however, English is widely spoken by the majority of people.
blocks.html: Tanzania's official languages are Swahili and English, and nearly everyone speaks Swahili. Within the tourism industry, however, most people speak English well.
